evals.prompt: I have two Podman containers to run on a host as systemd services: an API on its own and a background worker that should only start after the API is healthy. I want to manage them with Ansible using the containers.podman collection so the unit files are generated idempotently (real --check --diff), with hashed DB passwords injected as Podman secrets, a private-registry auth file, health checks, and restart-on-change. Show me the tasks.
evals.expected_output: Tasks using containers.podman.podman_container state: quadlet (quadlet_dir + quadlet_file_mode) for the API and the worker, podman_secret with no_log for the passwords then referenced via secrets: as 'name,type=env,target=ENV' strings, quadlet_options carrying the [Service] Restart=/TimeoutStartSec= and Environment=REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE= lines, the worker's [Unit] After=/Requires= webapp.service for ordering, healthcheck* params on the API, daemon_reload, then enable + (re)started based on registered .changed.

assertions.text: Uses containers.podman.podman_container with state: quadlet
Sets quadlet_dir (e.g. /etc/containers/systemd)
Uses containers.podman.podman_secret with no_log: true
References secrets via secrets: as '<name>,type=env,target=<ENV>' strings
Worker has quadlet_options with [Unit] After= pointing at the API .service unit
API uses first-class healthcheck: plus healthcheck_interval/timeout/retries (and start_period)
Has a daemon_reload: true task
Enable/start tasks use registered .changed to decide restarted vs started
quadlet_options contains [Service] Restart= and Environment=REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE=

evals.prompt: I want to run a Podman app inside a pod (not network=host) with its own named bridge network and a named persistent volume. Show me the ansible tasks using containers.podman to generate the .pod, .network, .volume and .container quadlets so they chain correctly and start in dependency order.
evals.expected_output: Tasks emitting podman_network state:quadlet, podman_volume state:quadlet, podman_pod state:quadlet, then podman_container state:quadlet with pod: <podname> joining the pod, plus unit ordering via quadlet_options [Unit] Requires=/After= on the generated .pod unit, then daemon_reload + enable in dependency order.

assertions.text: Uses podman_network with state: quadlet
Uses podman_volume with state: quadlet
Uses podman_pod with state: quadlet
Uses podman_container with state: quadlet AND pod: <podname>
Has a daemon_reload: true task
Enables units in dependency order: network/volume before pod before container
Container quadlet_options has [Unit] After=/Requires= the pod unit (e.g. <name>-pod.service)

evals.prompt: I have a vendor-provided quadlet bundle myapp.quadlets with three sections and three # FileName= comments. Install it onto a target LXC with Ansible and make sure systemd picks it up, with idempotent reruns. Don't generate the file, just install it.
evals.expected_output: Uses containers.podman.podman_quadlet state: present src: <path/to/myapp.quadlets> quadlet_dir: /etc/containers/systemd, relies on reload_systemd default true, notes Podman 6+ requirement for .quadlets and the # FileName= marker rule, and that local-file installs are idempotent via manifest comparison while URL src always reports changed.

assertions.text: Uses containers.podman.podman_quadlet (not a generator module like podman_container)
state: present
src: points to a .quadlets file
Notes Podman 6+ requirement for .quadlets bundles (in comments or task name)
Notes the # FileName= marker requirement for each section
Relies on reload_systemd default true OR explicitly sets it (does NOT require a separate daemon_reload task)
